Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Executive sign-off for 3yr rate lock + renewal protection (Acadia Health)

Team — attaching the latest term sheet and our deal model. Acadia is asking for a 3-year firm price lock on their standard hosted inference plan with two non-standard asks they want included in the contract: (1) an annual uplift cap of 8% (they requested 5% but pushed to 8 during negotiation), and (2) a renewal protection clause that guarantees the first renewal increase will not exceed 5% or CPI, whichever is lower, provided they meet committed usage.

Why now: Acadia is the top prospect in the health vertical for our Dedicated pipeline and wants multi-year predictability for budgeting. They committed to a 3-year minimum spend of $3.6M (yearly ramp) and will move to Dedicated if we agree to the lock & protections. Finance and Legal input needed for final approval.

Ask:
- Executive approval to grant a 3-year price lock with uplift cap of 8%/year, plus the renewal protection clause as described (first renewal capped at 5%/CPI lower).
- If approval is granted, authorize Deal Desk to sign term sheet subject to final legal redlines (attached).
- If not, please indicate acceptable counter (max uplift we can allow, or alternative guardrails).

Attachments: Acadia_TermSheet_v3.pdf, Acadia_RateModel_v3.xlsx

Cheers,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Principal Account Exec, Redwood Inference
(s) 415-555-0103

Subject: Re: Request: Executive sign-off for 3yr rate lock + renewal protection (Acadia Health)

Soojin / team — reviewed the attached model. Fiscal impact: granting an 8% annual uplift cap increases present value exposure vs. our baseline by ~9% over three years; downside scenario (usage drop to 60% year 3) reduces gross margin by ~7 points. We can approve conditionally if the following are included in the commercial terms:

1) A net revenue floor: Acadia must hit at least 85% of committed spend each year to keep the price lock intact; if they drop below, rate reversion to list pricing applies.
2) An overage policy: any usage above committed baseline should be invoiced at an overage rate set at list * 1.02 (no uplift).
3) Escrow clause for multi-year refund reserve of 5% to cover early termination clawback.

If Legal can sign off on these insertions, Finance will greenlight. Please incorporate into redlines and push back if Acadia refuses.

Laura Bennett
VP Finance, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Acadia_RateModel_v3_with_floors.xlsx (see sheet "Scenarios")
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 15:49:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Executive sign-off for 3yr rate lock + renewal protection (Acadia Health)

Team — reviewed term sheet and have proposed redlines (attached redlines_20261008.docx). Key legal items:

- Renewal protection: we can agree to cap the first renewal to the lesser of 5% or CPI, but only if we explicitly limit this to rate changes (per-unit price) and exclude changes driven by regulatory fees, third-party infra costs, or materially changed service scope.
- Require a mutual termination for convenience with 90 days notice and pro rata refund mechanics tied to the escrow reserve.
- Audit & compliance: Acadia must provide quarterly usage reports and permit a single annual audit to validate committed usage (we'll own cost if audit shows >5% variance in our favor, they pay if variance >5% in their favor).
- Security addendum: because they are healthcare, include SOC2 Type II attestation and a data handling clause referencing our Private deployment options.

I recommend we present this as a conditional approval to Execs with the Finance guardrails included. If Execs approve, Legal will push the redlines and prepare an approval memo.

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlines_20261008.docx

Subject: Re: Request: Executive sign-off for 3yr rate lock + renewal protection (Acadia Health)

Approved subject to Legal/Finance redlines and Deal Desk inserting a 12-month exit clause tied to the escrow mechanics. Final conditions I want on the approval memo:

- 3-year price lock granted with maximum uplift 8%/yr; first renewal capped to min(5%, CPI) as proposed by Legal.
- Net revenue floor of 85% per year; reversion to list pricing if floor not met.
- Escrow reserve 5% with defined pro rata refund on termination; Deal Desk to detail timing and triggers.
- Quarterly usage reviews and right to audit as per Legal.

Soojin, please proceed to share these terms with Acadia, and if they consent, instruct Deal Desk to issue signature-ready term sheet and route to me for countersignature. If the external party pushes back materially on any item, elevate.

Markus Klein
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
